Thursday Night Live: attendance, first-time guests, and promotional support.

This report compares October 2026 Thursday Night Live performance with July–September 2026 and the comparable 2025 period. It separates Rancho, Lakeside, and combined adult attendance; tracks first-time guests; and documents the frequency, clarity, and discoverability of TNL promotion.

What that means

Important: Oct. 16, 2025 was an app-launch outlier with 96 Connection Card submissions, 11 combined FTGs, and 29 decisions. It should not be treated as a normal marketing benchmark.

Promotional support

Promotion frequency, content clarity, and website presence

Promotion frequency, event-detail clarity, and website discoverability are important context variables. They may help explain performance differences, but they do not by themselves prove causation.

13
Instagram posts in the prior comparison period
July 31 through the end of October 2025, paired with a strong website presence. This corrects the earlier year typo.
14
Total TNL Instagram posts in 2026
Across the year to date.
6
TNL Instagram posts since Aug. 1, 2026
During the period most relevant to the current fall push.
10+
Illuminate posts
A single-night women’s event received more than ten social posts—an internal benchmark for what concentrated promotion can look like.

Quantity is only part of the issue

Even when TNL appears on social media, not every post functions as an event-acquisition asset. Promotional effectiveness depends on whether a post tells someone what is happening, when it is happening, where it is happening, and why they should come.

Website discoverability matters too

The prior comparison period had a strong website presence. In 2026, TNL has had little to no easily discoverable website presence, which shifts more of the information burden onto social media and the app.

Frequency

2026 has only six TNL posts since Aug. 1, while a single-night event like Illuminate received 10+ posts.

Clarity

Some TNL content appears optimized more for personality/engagement than for answering “Why should I come tonight?”

Findability

With little website presence, someone who misses the social post has no strong public destination to recover the event information.

Interpretation guardrail: These observations strengthen the case that TNL has received lighter and less event-specific promotional support in 2026. They should be treated as explanatory context—not as proof that marketing caused the attendance changes. Attendance can also be affected by seasonality, weather, competing events, service content, school schedules, and other factors.
Digital friction

Steps required to locate TNL information

The following maps the current website and app paths, including the number of actions required and the information shown in the two day-of screenshots.

45.2%
Average mobile scroll rate
Contentsquare’s current engagement benchmark says mobile users expose about 45.2% of a page on average.
74%
Viewing time in first 2 screens
Nielsen Norman Group found 74% of page-viewing time is spent in the first two screenfuls.
1.93%
Paid Facebook traffic CTR
Even campaigns specifically optimized to generate clicks average about a 1.93% CTR across industries in 2026.
Benchmark context: mobile users expose about 45.2% of a page on average, and Nielsen Norman Group found 74% of viewing time occurs within the first two screenfuls. These benchmarks provide context for evaluating how deeply event information is placed in the user journey.

Public website journey

Know or hear the phrase “October Nights”The user already has to possess some awareness before searching.
Go to SkylineChurch.orgThis is the logical public destination for someone who does not already use the app.
Open website searchThe user actively chooses to research the event.
Type “October Nights”High-intent behavior: this person is trying to find information.
Result: “Nothing Found”The public discovery journey ends. A motivated person cannot find the event through the obvious search path.

App journey — minimum 7 decision points

Already be a Skyline app userThis immediately biases the channel toward existing attenders.
Open the appThe user has to intentionally enter an internal Skyline channel.
Navigate to Home / News & EventsThe event is not the app’s sole focal point.
Scroll through the feedPotentially multiple swipes. Exact swipe count is not measurable from the screenshots alone, so this report does not invent one.
Notice and stop on October NightsThe user must decide the card is worth attention.
Read the date and event detailsThis is the moment the app should answer: “What is happening tonight?”
Receive next week’s information insteadOn two consecutive day-of screenshots, the featured card points to the following Thursday.
Tap “View Themes” / “Invite Oikos” to keep researchingIf the user suspects there is more information somewhere else, another tap is required.

Day-of information shown in the app

Screenshot takenWhat someone neededWhat the app displayedRisk

Observation: In both screenshots, the event card shown on Thursday displayed details for the following Thursday rather than that night. This creates ambiguity for a user trying to determine whether October Nights is happening that evening.

Discovery failure

The website search path ends in Nothing Found.

Friction failure

The app path requires multiple deliberate actions plus scrolling before details are reached.

Accuracy failure

For two consecutive Thursday screenshots, the day-of card advertised the following week.

Information access

Where TNL information currently appears

October Nights is designed to create attendance and first-time guests, but the strongest event information currently lives inside an app primarily used by existing attenders.

Current acquisition funnel

Already knows Skyline
↓
Has downloaded / uses the Skyline app
↓
Opens News & Events
↓
Scrolls far enough to see October Nights
↓
Opens the card
↓
Only then sees the theme / invite opportunity

Why this matters

1
People do not research hard for optional events.Digital behavior consistently shows shallow scanning, especially on mobile. Important information needs to be high, visible, and easy to act on.
2
Day-of social works best as a reminder.It should reinforce awareness that already exists, not be the first time most people hear about the event.
3
The website should be the public source of truth.If someone searches the event and gets “Nothing Found,” the acquisition path is broken.

Website: searching “October Nights” returns “Nothing Found.”

App: detailed, polished event information is available once someone finds the card.

App: weekly themes and Oikos language are present—but primarily inside an insider channel.

Documented pattern: detailed TNL information is concentrated in the app, while public website discoverability is limited and the two day-of screenshots displayed the following week’s event details.
Recommended fix

Run one repeatable seven-day promotion cycle.

Do not create six unrelated campaigns. Build one predictable rhythm that repeatedly moves people from awareness → interest → invitation → attendance.

Friday / Saturday
Recap + tease

Show what happened, then immediately reveal why next Thursday is worth attending.

Monday
Full reveal

Theme, food/activity, time, location, kids info, and one clear invitation CTA.

Tuesday
Oikos push

Give attenders one easy-to-share graphic, Reel, or text invite.

Wednesday
24-hour reminder

Social + app + email. Make tomorrow's experience unmistakably clear.

Thursday AM
Tonight

Simple, practical reminder with location, time, theme, and invite language.

Thursday PM
Live proof

Stories, short clips, atmosphere, and “come next week” messaging.

Website

Create one permanent public landing page: /thursday or /octobernights. Every channel links to it.

Social

Move from isolated posts to a deliberate weekly campaign. Day-of becomes a reminder, not the entire strategy.

App

Keep the app as the insider activation channel: equip existing Skyline people to invite, share, and bring their Oikos.

Measurement

Judge the campaign on incremental growth—not raw attendance.

The right question is not “Was Thursday busy?” It is “Did the additional spend create incremental attendance, FTGs, and decisions beyond what a normal Thursday already produces?”

Adult attendancePrimary attendance KPI. Excludes Kids, High School, and volunteers.
Adult attendance growthTrack week-over-week and against the Jul–Sep adult baseline.
Identifiable FTGsPrimary acquisition outcome.
Connect CardsMeasures engagement and response.
SalvationsTrack separately from recommitments.
RecommitmentsTrack separately from first-time decisions.
30-day FTG returnShows whether acquisition is becoming retention.
Cost per incremental FTGBest ROI measure for an acquisition-oriented event strategy.
Recommended top KPI: Incremental first-time guests per $1,000 of October Nights spending.
Data & methodology

Attendance: Skyline Google Drive → Updated 2026 Attendance and 2025 Attendance. Every attendance comparison in this report uses Thursday adult attendees only, shown separately for Rancho and Lakeside and then combined. Kids, High School, and volunteers are excluded.

Connection Cards / FTGs / Decisions: Planning Center People → active Connection Card form. First-time guests use the campus-specific workflow-backed fields on the Connection Card: Rancho FTGs are counted only from “FIRST time visiting the Rancho Campus,” Lakeside FTGs only from “FIRST time visiting the Lakeside Campus,” and Combined is the deduplicated total of both; decisions count physical-campus salvation + recommitment responses, deduplicated by person on each date. Historical form-date attribution is used instead of current workflow-card stage because workflow cards can move after the original visit.

2025 exceptions: Thanksgiving and Christmas Day were excluded as normal Thursday service comparisons where the attendance sheet identifies no regular Thursday service. Oct. 16, 2025 is flagged as an app-launch outlier.

Promotional-frequency observations: internal social-content count supplied for this report. Prior comparison period is treated as 2025 (correcting an earlier typo that said 2026): 13 Instagram posts from July 31 through end of October, with stronger website presence. For 2026: 14 total TNL Instagram posts, six since Aug. 1, little-to-no website presence, two pastor fit-check videos, one pastor walkout-song video, and 10+ posts for Illuminate as an internal frequency comparison.

Digital behavior references used in the underlying analysis:
• Contentsquare 2026 engagement benchmark: mobile scroll rate 45.2%; desktop 50.5%.
• Nielsen Norman Group scrolling/attention research: 57% of viewing time above the fold; 74% within the first two screenfuls.
• WordStream 2026 Facebook traffic-campaign benchmark: 1.93% average CTR across industries.
• Eventbrite / Sprout Social event-promotion and social-timing guidance.
